overview: 3SBio Inc. is a leading Chinese biopharmaceutical company (Cayman-incorporated, HKEX-listed) that researches, develops, manufactures and markets biologics and small-molecule drugs, with legacy strength in hematology (TPIAO, the world's only commercialized rhTPO), nephrology (EPIAO/SEPO rhEPO), autoimmune disease (Yisaipu, a TNF-alpha inhibitor) and consumer dermatology (Mandi minoxidil). The Group is transitioning from a mature, VBP-pressured legacy-biologics business toward a global innovative-drug/out-licensing model, highlighted by a 2025 landmark deal licensing its PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody (707/SSGJ-707) to Pfizer. It operates almost entirely in Mainland China commercially (11,000+ hospitals) with growing export/out-licensing exposure to 39+ overseas markets, plus a CDMO business including an Italian manufacturing subsidiary (Sirton).

business_model.summary: Revenue is generated from (1) sales of in-house biopharmaceuticals (TPIAO, EPIAO/SEPO, Yisaipu, Cipterbin, Mandi) sold mainly to distributors servicing Mainland China hospitals, (2) CDMO contract manufacturing services, and (3) increasingly, out-licensing/milestone income from partnering proprietary pipeline assets with multinational pharma (Pfizer). FY2025 was transformed by a one-off RMB9,425.9 million out-license/option fee from Pfizer for 707, which made up more than half of total revenue; excluding it, core biopharmaceutical product sales actually fell 10.3% YoY (RMB8,006.4m vs RMB8,927.9m) due to Volume-Based Procurement (VBP) price cuts and NRDL-related pricing pressure. Product revenue is largely non-recurring-contract/transactional (hospital purchases via distributors) rather than subscription-like, while out-licensing income is lumpy and milestone/royalty-driven going forward.

revenue_streams.name: Biopharmaceutical product sales (TPIAO, EPIAO/SEPO, Yisaipu, Cipterbin, Mandi, etc.)
Out-licensing / milestone income (Pfizer 707 deal)
revenue_streams.trend: one-off in FY2025; future milestones/royalties lumpy and uncertain

revenue_streams.name: CDMO contract manufacturing
revenue_streams.trend: growing (+46.3% in FY2025 off a small base)

business_model.customer_type: B2B/institutional - hospitals, distributors and medical institutions in Mainland China (11,000+ touchpoints) for commercial products; global biopharma partners (e.g., Pfizer) for out-licensing; some B2C/retail for Mandi (OTC, e-commerce)
business_model.geographic_mix: Overwhelmingly Mainland China for product sales; products additionally exported/sold in 39 overseas markets (e.g., Thailand, Brazil, Philippines, Pakistan); out-licensing deal value (Pfizer) is global ex-China rights with China retained/optioned

main_competitors: Akeso Inc. (ivonescimab, partnered with Summit Therapeutics - leading PD-1/VEGF bispecific)
Multinational originators (Roche, Amgen, J&J) in legacy biologics classes facing domestic biosimilar substitution
competitive_position.market_position: Dominant/legacy leader in niche mature biologics: TPIAO holds ~60% value share / ~28% volume share of China's thrombocytopenia treatment market (world's only commercial rhTPO); the two rhEPO products hold ~40% share of China's rhEPO market (market leader for over two decades); Mandi holds a dominant position in China's hair-loss drug OTC market. In the emerging PD-1/VEGF bispecific category (707), 3SBio is a credible but not first-mover player - Akeso's ivonescimab is the clear category leader with multiple positive Phase III OS readouts and a pending US BLA (PDUFA Nov 2026), and BioNTech/BMS's pumitamig is also advancing rapidly; the Pfizer deal nonetheless validates 3SBio's R&D platform and provides capital/credibility.

moat_factors.description: TPIAO is the only commercialized rhTPO globally, giving pricing power and entrenched physician/hospital adoption despite VBP pressure
Extensive in-house sales force (~2,900 staff) and 20+ year relationships across 11,000+ hospitals support continued share even as pricing erodes
Mandi dominant OTC minoxidil brand, though this business is being spun off/divested

moat_factors.factor: R&D platform credibility validated by Pfizer
moat_factors.description: The $1.25bn upfront, largest-ever for a China-origin drug out-license, signals platform quality (CLF2 bispecific technology) but does not guarantee competitive leadership versus faster-moving domestic rivals
NMPA approvals and NRDL listings create switching friction, but China's VBP and biosimilar-tendering system is explicitly designed to erode incumbents' pricing power over time

weaknesses: Core legacy biologics portfolio (TPIAO, EPIAO, Yisaipu) is mature and shrinking under VBP/NRDL price cuts, not a growth driver
Late-mover position in the hot PD-1/VEGF bispecific category relative to Akeso/ivonescimab and BioNTech/BMS's pumitamig
High customer/product concentration - a small number of legacy drugs still account for the bulk of organic revenue
FY2025 reported profitability is overwhelmingly a one-off licensing event, not a repeatable earnings run-rate
Planned Mandi spin-off removes a profitable, cash-generative consumer business from the group

growth_drivers: Milestone and royalty cash flows from the Pfizer 707 licensing deal (up to USD4.8bn in further milestones plus tiered double-digit royalties, plus a China commercialization option worth up to USD150m)

Pipeline of 24-27 innovative drug candidates (antibodies/fusion proteins, small molecules) across oncology, autoimmune/inflammatory disease, nephrology, dermatology and metabolic disease, several at NDA/Phase III stage (608 IL-17A, 611 IL-4R, 613 IL-1beta, 610 IL-5, 601A anti-VEGF)

Continued "dual-track" strategy of in-house R&D plus external out-licensing partnerships to monetize pipeline assets globally, following the record Pfizer precedent and a broader 2025 boom in China biotech out-licensing (reported >US$130bn cumulative deal value, >150 transactions)
New product launches/NRDL inclusion (NuPIAO, Yisaituo, Liporaxel) to refresh the commercial portfolio as legacy products face pricing pressure

Secular tailwind: Chinese government elevated biopharma to a national "emerging pillar industry" under the 15th Five-Year Plan, with new Commercial Health Insurance Innovative Drug List designed to reward high-value innovative drugs outside basic NRDL price caps
Global expansion - products already sold in 39 overseas markets; TPIAO pursuing its first registrational trial outside China (US FDA-approved CLDT bridging trial, July 2026)
CDMO segment growth (+46.3% in FY2025) as a smaller diversification lever

business.description: Legacy biologics (TPIAO, EPIAO/SEPO, Yisaipu) sales fell 10.3% in FY2025 due to VBP tenders and healthcare insurance pricing policy, and management explicitly flags continuing VBP pressure on Yisaipu

707 is behind Akeso/Summit's ivonescimab (multiple positive Phase III OS data, BLA under FDA review) and BioNTech/BMS's pumitamig; failure to differentiate clinically could limit 707's ultimate commercial value to Pfizer and future royalty/milestone realization
27 pipeline candidates span early to late stage; clinical trial failures, delays or disappointing Phase III data (particularly for 611, 610, 613, 601A) would directly impact the growth narrative

Removing the profitable, high-margin consumer dermatology business via distribution-in-specie and separate HKEx listing shrinks the post-spin-off group's cash-generative base and dilutes a reliable earnings stream

financial.description: FY2025 revenue (RMB17.7bn) and net income (RMB8.5bn) are massively inflated by a one-off RMB9.4bn Pfizer upfront/option licensing fee; using FY2025 as a valuation base year without normalizing for this is likely to materially overstate sustainable earnings power
Pfizer share subscription (31.1m shares) and a December 2025 placement (105.2m shares, ~HK$3.1bn raised at a discount) materially increased share count within the year
Future milestone and royalty payments from Pfizer will be USD-denominated against an RMB-reporting, HKD-quoted company, creating translation exposure

regulatory.risk: Volume-Based Procurement (VBP) and NRDL price negotiations
regulatory.description: China's VBP tendering regime and NRDL renegotiation cycles systematically compress prices on mature biologics/biosimilars (precedent: national VBP rounds have cut prices 40-50%+ in other categories); 3SBio's legacy portfolio remains directly exposed
Company changed auditor from EY (15+ year incumbent) to KPMG effective June 2026 AGM; routine, but a transition risk to monitor for any control findings in upcoming audits

regulatory.risk: Cross-border licensing/antitrust and biosecurity policy risk
regulatory.description: Large cross-border biotech licensing deals involving Chinese innovative drugs and US/multinational partners are subject to evolving geopolitical, export-control and biosecurity policy scrutiny in both China and the US

macro.description: National and local medical insurance fund pressures continue to drive aggressive price-control policy across the industry
Could affect the pace and terms of future China-to-multinational out-licensing deals, a key growth lever for 3SBio post-Pfizer
RMB-denominated financials and multi-currency (USD licensing proceeds, HKD listing) create translation and reporting complexity

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Chinese biopharma was elevated to a national 'emerging pillar industry' under the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030); 2025 was a record year for China-origin biotech out-licensing (reportedly >US$130bn cumulative deal value, >150 deals, ~US$7bn total upfronts), reflecting rising multinational recognition of Chinese innovation quality. China's biosimilars market is projected to grow from roughly US$5.5bn (2026) to US$23.6bn (2035), a ~17.5% CAGR, but with intensifying price competition.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate - healthcare/biopharma demand is relatively defensive, but company-specific revenue is highly lumpy given large one-off licensing fees and milestone payment timing; core legacy product demand is stable but pricing is structurally declining
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity to rates; indirect sensitivity via cost of debt (modest bank borrowings ~RMB2.55bn) and via valuation multiples applied to a biotech growth narrative
key_input_costs: Biologics manufacturing inputs (cell culture media, bioreactor consumables)
Clinical trial costs (scaling with expanding late-stage pipeline)
Staff costs for ~2,900 sales/marketing employees and ~840 R&D scientists

recent_developments.event: Announced and then completed (effective 24 July 2025) an exclusive global (ex-China) licensing agreement with Pfizer for PD-1/VEGF bispecific 707: USD1.25bn upfront, up to USD4.8bn in milestones, tiered double-digit royalties, plus a China commercialization option worth up to USD150m - the largest upfront payment in the history of China biotech out-licensing
Pfizer completed subscription of 31,142,500 new shares at HK$25.2055/share (~17% discount to spot), becoming a strategic shareholder (~1.28% stake)
Placed 105,169,500 new shares to institutional investors at HK$29.62/share, raising ~HK$3.1bn net, at a ~6.5% discount to spot - triggered a notable share price pullback on dilution concerns

Filed for HKEx main board spin-off listing of Mandi Inc. (hair-loss/consumer dermatology subsidiary) via distribution-in-specie plus a global offering; HKEx confirmed the Group may proceed; EGM circular process underway into 2026, final listing/EGM outcome not yet confirmed as of October 2026

Multiple NMPA approvals/filings progressed across the pipeline: 608 (anti-IL-17A) approved Feb 2026; SSS20 (Eltrombopag) approved March 2026; 611 (anti-IL-4R) NDA accepted Feb 2026; 613 (anti-IL-1beta) approved for acute gouty arthritis Aug 2026; TPIAO received FDA approval (July 2026) to begin its first-ever registrational trial outside China
Shareholders approved appointment of KPMG as new auditor, replacing EY after 15+ years, effective from the 2026 AGM

Revenue +94.3% YoY to RMB17.70bn and net profit +305.8% YoY to RMB8.48bn, almost entirely attributable to the one-off RMB9.43bn Pfizer out-license/option income; core biopharmaceutical product sales declined 10.3% YoY on VBP/NRDL pricing pressure

Revenue +3.9% YoY to RMB4.53bn; reported net profit -15.6% YoY to RMB1.15bn (prior-year period benefited from early Pfizer-deal-related fair value/non-operating gains), while net profit adjusted for non-operating items rose 26.5% YoY to RMB1.44bn; gross margin compressed slightly to 83.8% from 85.3%

Stock declined sharply from 2025 highs (reportedly down roughly 40-45% over the trailing year per multiple data aggregators) amid dilution from the share placement, normalization expectations after the one-off FY2025 licensing boost, and profit-taking after the post-Pfizer-deal rally

guidance.as_of: FY2025 Annual Report (30 March 2026) and H1 2026 Interim Report

items.notes: Management does not issue formal numeric revenue/EPS guidance; qualitative outlook emphasizes continuing the 'dual-track' strategy (in-house R&D plus external licensing) and that 707 milestone payments from Pfizer will be recognized 'in stages' as development/regulatory/sales milestones are achieved over coming years, implying lumpy, non-linear future licensing income rather than a smooth run-rate

items.target: Up to USD4.8bn in additional development/regulatory/sales milestones, plus tiered double-digit royalties on ex-China sales, plus up to USD150m option/exercise fee for China rights
items.notes: USD1.25bn upfront already received and recognized in FY2025; remaining consideration is entirely contingent on clinical/regulatory/commercial success and is non-guaranteed

items.target: ~80% of net proceeds from both the Pfizer share subscription (~HK$785m) and the December 2025 placement (~HK$3,115m) earmarked for R&D/clinical pipeline advancement and manufacturing capacity; ~20% for general corporate/working capital purposes
items.period: To be utilized over next 3 years
items.notes: As of FY2025 year-end only a small fraction (~HK$70m of subscription proceeds, ~HK$30m of placement proceeds) had been utilized, with the bulk still earmarked for deployment through 2028

items.target: Complete HKEx main-board listing of Mandi Inc. via distribution-in-specie plus global offering
items.period: In progress through 2026 (EGM/listing timeline not finalized as of this report)
items.notes: Conditional on shareholder approval and HKEx listing committee sign-off; outcome and final timing remained unconfirmed as of October 2026

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Dr. Lou Jing characterized 2025 as a 'milestone year' driven by the Pfizer collaboration and record revenue/profit, while explicitly flagging that future milestone cash will come in stages. Management's FY2025 and H1 2026 outlook statements emphasize a 'dual-track' strategy (independent R&D plus external partnerships/out-licensing), continued focus on accelerating market access for newly approved products (Yisaituo, Liporaxel, NuPIAO), and transitioning the Group 'from scale to quality and from imitation to innovation' under China's 15th Five-Year Plan designation of biopharma as a national pillar industry. No explicit FY2026 revenue or profit targets were disclosed.

bull_case: The Pfizer deal (largest-ever China biotech out-license, USD1.25bn upfront already banked, up to USD4.8bn more in milestones plus royalties) validates 3SBio's R&D platform, de-risks the balance sheet, and creates a multi-year string of potential milestone catalysts

Deep, broad pipeline (24-27 candidates) spanning oncology, autoimmune disease, nephrology and metabolic disease provides multiple shots at further value-creating out-licensing deals, replicating the Pfizer playbook amid a historically hot China biotech licensing market

Dominant/entrenched positions in niche legacy categories (TPIAO ~60% value share, rhEPO ~40% share) generate a durable, if slow-growing, cash-generative base and extensive hospital distribution network that supports commercialization of newer approvals
Strong balance sheet post-deal/post-placement: net current assets rose to ~RMB18.3bn and current ratio to ~5.1x at FY2025 year-end, funding continued R&D investment without near-term financing risk

Favorable policy tailwinds - China's 15th Five-Year Plan designates biopharma a national pillar industry, and the new Commercial Health Insurance Innovative Drug List offers a pricing pathway for innovative drugs outside basic NRDL caps
bear_case: FY2025's blowout revenue/profit figures are overwhelmingly a one-off licensing event (RMB9.4bn of RMB17.7bn revenue); using FY2025 as a steady-state valuation base year substantially overstates normalized earnings power, and consensus already models a sharp earnings decline in subsequent years

Core legacy biologics business is shrinking, not growing - product sales fell 10.3% in FY2025 under VBP/NRDL pricing pressure, and this structural headwind on TPIAO, EPIAO/SEPO and Yisaipu is likely to persist as China continues aggressive volume-based procurement rounds

3SBio is a later entrant in the hotly competitive PD-1/VEGF bispecific category - Akeso/Summit's ivonescimab already has multiple positive Phase III overall-survival readouts and a BLA under FDA review, while BioNTech/BMS's pumitamig is also advancing quickly, raising the risk that 707's ultimate clinical/commercial differentiation (and thus the realized value of Pfizer's contingent milestones) falls short of the deal's headline potential

Material share dilution (Pfizer subscription plus a discounted HK$3.1bn placement) coincided with a sharp share price decline (reportedly ~40-45% over the trailing year), reflecting market skepticism about sustaining the post-deal re-rating and concerns about future EPS trajectory

Planned Mandi spin-off removes a profitable, cash-generative consumer dermatology business from the group, shrinking the diversified earnings base the remaining entity can rely on while pipeline assets mature
